statements.venue: Opening statement as ranking member, House Education and Workforce Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development hearing "Building an AI-Ready America: Higher Education in the Age of AI"
statements.quote: We need clear guardrails to ensure AI strengthens education rather than weakens it.

statements.reason: She discusses risks of AI in education (bias, student data, inequality) but not catastrophic risk.

notes: All six required web searches ran this time, plus one more on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, for seven in total. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced 24 September 2026): the FastDemocracy cosponsor page lists 12 cosponsors and Adams is not among them. A Forkast article (https://forkast.news/progressive-democrats-establish-prohibitionist-left-flank-on-artificial-superintelligence/) also does not mention her. Congress.gov could not be checked (it returned HTTP 403 in the earlier attempt), so whether she co-sponsored remains unconfirmed by an official source. No House letter about AI risk led by her was found; the multi-signer letters were excluded as the House instructions say. A search result says she signed a 2025 letter led by Rep. Deborah Ross that asked for the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws to be removed from the defense bill (https://ross.house.gov/_cache/files/4/7/47241f79-476e-4384-9644-a6d6d1c923f3/0B2655828FC164F250E5A6635481C7CCCB14B0E9EA3B3E4F6A397519FDFD7FF1.final-ndaa-ai-moratorium-women-and-children-letter.pdf). I could not extract the PDF text, so her signature and the letter's content are not verified. That letter concerns state regulation, not a pause on AI development, so it does not affect any position. The earlier attempt opened the adams.house.gov press release listing (20 November 2025 to 28 October 2026) and found no titles or excerpts mentioning AI. That check read listing excerpts only, so it missed the 20 March 2026 energy release, which mentions AI in its body. The quotes above came through a page-reading tool that returns extracted text, so a reviewer should confirm the exact punctuation against the source pages. Other results matching 'Adams' and AI concerned Elizabeth M. Adams, a different person, and were excluded.
